source.title: The Common Intuition to Transfer Learning Can Win or Lose: Case Studies for Linear Regression
source.authors: Yehuda Dar; Daniel LeJeune; Richard Baraniuk

page_placements.theme: Source interpolation and pretraining affect target generalization

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some mathematical notation is affected by PDF text extraction, but the relevant findings are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and evaluates test-error curves in linear regression, a different model setting and method from the cited deep-network studies.
record.gate_note: The study sweeps the number of learned parameters and reports target-task test errors for minimum-norm regression, ridge regression, and transfer learning. Cited double-descent results are not counted as the study's own results. It does not sweep training epochs or target sample size. Many plotted curves have no numerical values in the text, so those outcomes are recorded qualitatively.
record.test_reason: In linear-regression transfer learning, the study derives and simulates its own target test-error curves against parameter count d (150 runs per point). These include the minimum-norm (ML2N) peak at d≈n, its removal by optimally tuned ridge, and a peak inherited from the source threshold that optimal transfer tuning does not remove. The ML2N and ridge formulas restate known results (refs 3, 18, 29), so most of the novelty is in the transfer setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that intuitive transfer with H̃=I can outperform using the true task relation in overparameterized regimes. They add that intuitive transfer degrades at very high overparameterization, which the LMMSE transfer solution fixes, questioning the common transfer-learning design.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and evaluates linear-regression transfer learning and minimum-norm/ridge solutions, rather than reproducing the original deep-network model-size experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The transfer-induced peak depends on whether the source interpolation threshold lies in the target underparameterized or overparameterized regime. Outcomes also vary with task relation, relation noise, and misspecification; the paper reports differences between using the true H and using the identity operator.

fits_no_version.finding: Transfer from an ML2N source carries a test-error peak into the target at the source interpolation threshold, but only when that threshold lies in the target's overparameterized regime (n<ñ). With n>ñ there is no significant peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A source model's double-descent peak propagates to a transfer-learned target model only in the target's overparameterized regime.

record.peer_reviewed: SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science
record.problems: The reported numerical curves are primarily figures, without stated error bars or confidence intervals. The tested models are linear regression, not deep networks; epoch-wise and target-sample-size sweeps are absent.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results omitted. Per-noise-level plotted curves are not separately cataloged where the text reports the same qualitative outcome and supplies no separate numerical value.

untested.parts: All of it: no deep networks.
All of it: no training-time sweeps.
All of it: target sample size n is fixed per figure (64 or 128), not swept near the threshold.
Model classes other than linear regression.
The label-noise dependence of the target peak (σϵ² is not swept), and genuine multiple descent within one curve.

missing.what: Corollary 4.4: optimally tuned transfer beats tuned ridge if ση²+dσξ²/(|d−ñ|−1)<b, and never at d∈{ñ−1,ñ,ñ+1}. This is a non-asymptotic condition on the peak's location.
The well-specified statement that all methods have higher overparameterized than underparameterized error.

record.verdict_notes: The double-descent content is mostly a baseline for a transfer-learning study. The ML2N formula (3.2) is stated as a special case of refs 3 and 7, and ridge removing the peak follows refs 18 and 29. These remain the study's own analytic and empirical curves, so they are kept as rows. Curve values are figure-only, with no error bars.

versions.untested_parts: Increasing target training sample size near the interpolation threshold.
Model classes other than linear regression.
Whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.

Whether label noise or variance drives the peak; triple or multiple descent beyond the reported additional source-threshold peak; and whether optimally tuned regularization removes peaks across methods generally.
Recounting complexity by effective parameters and whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: minimum ℓ2-norm (ML2N) solution to linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed target test error as parameterization d varies relative to target sample count n.
rows.value: The error has a peak around the underparameterized-to-overparameterized threshold; the paper gives it as infinite for n − 1 ≤ d ≤ n + 1, with separate formulas below and above that interval.
rows.note: The equations and the authors' discussion describe the peak in the target-task minimum-norm error as model parameterization varies.
rows.check: The error does fall again past the peak, but in the well-specified isotropic case it tends to σϵ²+b. The authors state that overparameterized errors are usually higher than underparameterized errors here (Sec. 5, Fig. 1a). The second descent never beats the underparameterized optimum, so 'observed' overstates it.

rows.subject: minimum ℓ2-norm (ML2N) solution to linear regression
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated target test error as d varies under the paper's misspecification model.

conditions.value: Assumptions 4–5; polynomial reduction with a = 2.5, q = 500, ρ = 2

rows.value: The paper states that overparameterized models can achieve the best generalization performance; the plotted curve is in Figure 1b.
rows.note: The paper describes misspecification as significantly changing test-error behavior with parameterization.
rows.check: None. Under misspecification the best error lies at d/n>1 (Sec. 5, Figs 1b, 9).

rows.subject: optimally tuned ridge regression
rows.operation_detail: Compared expected target test error across parameterization levels with optimally tuned ridge regression.

conditions.value: isotropic target features and isotropic Gaussian parameter prior

rows.value: The paper states that optimally tuned ridge regression resolves the minimum-norm solution's generalization-error peak.
rows.note: The ridge regularization parameter is analytically optimally tuned for the expected test error.
rows.check: This reproduces a known result (refs 18, 29) analytically and empirically. The link is acceptable.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.3, Equation (4.11), Figure 1a and accompanying discussion; Appendix D.1.

rows.subject: intuitive transfer learning solution (3.3)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated target test error across d using optimally tuned transfer regularization.

conditions.value: sufficiently low; Figure 1a shows several ση² values

rows.baseline: Minimum ℓ2-norm and optimally tuned ridge curves
rows.value: Transfer learning can resolve the target minimum-norm peak and lower error over most parameterization levels, but produces another peak around the source-task interpolation threshold.
rows.uncertainty: Empirical errors averaged over 150 experiments; no error bar or CI stated.
rows.note: The paper attributes the additional peak to transfer from a source model whose own minimum-norm solution has a peak.
rows.check: This is one relocated peak, not multiple descent: the target ML2N peak is resolved and a new peak appears at d≈ñ. Optimally tuned transfer regularization still gives infinite error at d∈{ñ−1,ñ,ñ+1} (Thm 4.2). The row bears on 'disappears under optimally tuned regularization' only for this regularizer.

rows.subject: intuitive transfer learning solution (3.3)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the source-task interpolation threshold's location with the target test-error curve as d varies.
rows.measure: Target test error near the source-task interpolation threshold
rows.value: The paper states there is no significant target test-error peak around the source threshold when that threshold lies in the target underparameterized regime.
rows.uncertainty: Empirical errors averaged over 150 experiments; no error bar or CI stated.
rows.note: This is a condition-dependent absence of the additional transfer-induced peak, not an absence of the target-task minimum-norm peak.
rows.check: This concerns where the source-inherited peak appears, not any version's peak. Move it to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: intuitive transfer learning solution (3.3)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated target test error across d in misspecified transfer-learning settings.
rows.value: The paper states that overparameterized models can achieve the best generalization performance in misspecified settings.
rows.note: The result shows that misspecification changes the error-versus-parameterization behavior; the text does not characterize this as a general noise-driven or multiple-descent result.
rows.check: This is wrongly linked to V6. The finding is that overparameterized models reach the best error under misspecification (Fig. 4), which bears on V4. State is observed, not partial.
